name: ell_defect_and_d_cb
statement: For a sign fibre A subset {+-1}^r the entropy defect is ell(A) = r - log_2|A|. d_cb(A) is the minimum signed-selector residual rank after optimizing over ALL coordinate bases drawn from the full dual of A: pick a coordinate basis, pick for each full-dual form a signed basis selector, require all assignment residuals to lie in one common space R, and minimize dim R over basis and selector choices.
notes: S6 uses ell and d_cb throughout without re-deriving them; the quantifier 'optimizing over all coordinate bases in the full dual' is the load-bearing part (it is what makes d_cb weaker than a fixed-basis d(H)).

name: unrooted_linear_selector_target_S6_1
statement: Target (1): d_cb(A) <= C*ell(A) for every spanning full-closed antipodal sign fibre A subset {+-1}^r, with an absolute C, uniformly in the real/no-wrap setting AND in the odd finite fields F_p used by the centered-moment argument.
notes: Field uniformity (R and odd F_p simultaneously) is part of the demand, not a convenience. This is the 'clean sufficient form' of the missing global step; S6's verdict is that the completed corank-3/4 theorems do not supply it.

name: conditional_defect_L_Q_given_W
statement: For a sign basis (W,Q) on a finite support A, with W the incoming sign boundary and Q the private sign basis of size q, the conditional defect is L_{Q|W} = |Q| - H(Q|W) (tag 2). Here H is base-2 entropy of Q under the uniform measure on A conditioned on W.
notes: L is CONDITIONAL, not the block's unconditional defect; S9's Theorem 1 proof marks the exact step where this distinction is used (S9 lines 163-164).

name: rooted_connector_rigidity_target_S6_3
statement: Target (3), the rooted version needed by the recursive block-tree proof: with R_< subset span W the residual space already paid by ancestors, the private cyclic forms must admit a selector space R with (i) dim((R+R_<)/R_<) <= C*L_{Q|W} and (ii) R cap span W subset R_< (connector absorption). Boundary-only forms are assigned to the parent.
notes: S6 states the purpose of clause (ii) verbatim: 'Without the second condition, a boundary residual can be paid again at every descendant.' Conditional defects are then said to telescope with one global constant supplied by recursive_paired_block_tree_entropy.md (a file NOT reproduced in the dossier and absent from every machine this campaign controls).

name: evaluation_rado_bound_S6_4
statement: Intrinsic stronger sufficient theorem (4): q_ev(A) >= r - C*ell(A). By the Rado certificate lemma, (4) implies (1). The relaxed activation-cell theorem in the research report is stronger still but is not logically necessary.
notes: q_ev is the evaluation rank/Rado quantity defined in the synthesis pages, not re-defined here. The same 2.40942 constant floor applies to (4) as to (1).

name: nae_three_circuit_product_constant_floor
statement: The product of t NAE three-circuits has ell = t*log_2(4/3) and d_cb = t. Hence every constant in (1) or (4) must be at least 1/log_2(4/3) = 2.40942... (tag 5). The same family satisfies the exponential bound (17) with large slack, because a two-shadow maximum matching has only linear size whereas 4^ell = (4^beta)^t.
source: dossier p.114 (S6 lines 50-55); audit item 1 at p.122 (S6 lines 434-438)
notes: beta = log_2(4/3) = 0.4150. Any proof strategy must tolerate C >= 2.40942; a claimed constant below that is refuted by this family. Exact, not asymptotic.

name: layer_iii_transfer_still_required
statement: After (1) there remains a second, probabilistic endpoint: one must insert the resulting component estimate into the required-order centered moment, or prove the random-normal tail / JSS endpoint inversion directly. Even a proof of (1) should not by itself be described as a completed proof of the determinant conjecture until that transfer is written out.
notes: S6's own honesty clause. Records that the deterministic Layer-II target and the Layer-III transfer are two separate unwritten pieces.

name: irreducible_cyclic_core_location
statement: After removing (a) acyclic tails and globally compatible private pivots, (b) every nonsingleton Gale-flag layer, (c) circuit trees, sparse-cycle blocks, bounded/growing stars, low-rank shared-form blocks and the stable-set/poset/median classes, and (d) boundary-closed homogeneous cyclic cores of relation corank <= 4, the first homogeneous survivor is a singleton-layer strongly connected component of relation corank >= 5. Equivalently every admissible determinant matching and feedback set has feedback residual rank kappa(T,F) >> ell (tag 6), and no basis exchange turns all remaining forms into distinct private pivots.
notes: S6 says 'the audited reductions imply the following' - it rests on the Layer-I classification reproduced elsewhere in the dossier, not on anything proved on pp.113-155. Nonroot blocks carry an additional affine obstruction: conditioning on the boundary turns homogeneous equations into target-dependent atoms, and the homogeneous corank-four theorem does not control their conditional defect.

name: more_finite_low_corank_endpoints_do_not_bridge
statement: Finishing further finite low-corank endpoints cannot by itself bridge to arbitrary singular mechanisms. A local target-uniform atom bound alone does not establish the absorption statement in (3). The necessary new information is global basis exchange / entropy in a high-corank cyclic block.
notes: Kills the 'just do corank 5, then 6, ...' program as a route to the global step. Stated as a structural obstruction, not merely as a difficulty.

name: weighted_two_shadow_compression_thm1
statement: Theorem 1 (S6). Let K = R, or K = F_p with p > r odd. Let h_a in K^r and S = {x in {+-1}^r : h_a.x in {+-1} for every a}, |S| = 2^{r-ell}. Discard rows equal to signed coordinate forms; for each remaining row let E_a = supp h_a, so |E_a| >= 2. There is a set C subset [r] with |C| <= C_0*4^ell (tag 8) and |E_a \ C| <= 1 for every a (tag 9). One may take an absolute numerical C_0, for example C_0 = 32.
source: dossier p.115 (S6 lines 103-129); audit p.128 (S7 lines 30-46)
notes: S7 sharpens the admissible constant to C_0 = 9. Improves the old two-shadow core size from O((1+ell)4^ell) to O(4^ell). NO full-closure and NO antipodality hypothesis is used. Field condition p > r odd is required (it feeds u <= r < p in the finite-group LO step).

name: psi_two_target_atom_bound
statement: psi(u) = min{3/4, 2^{1-u}*C(u, floor(u/2))} <= min{3/4, 2/sqrt(u)} (tag 12). For u = 2 the 3/4 bound is the nondegenerate-parallelogram bound; for u >= 3 it is the ordinary two-atom Littlewood-Offord bound. Over F_p invoke the finite-group one-point Littlewood-Offord theorem: when u < p and all coefficients are nonzero, each atom is at most the central-binomial mass; a union bound over the two targets gives the same psi.
source: dossier p.116 (S6 lines 174-186); audit pp.131-132 (S7 lines 139-184)
notes: The bound must be uniform in the target center b, in the coefficients, and in all earlier block values - all three quantifiers are used by the reverse-exposure argument.

name: reverse_exposure_triangular_product
statement: Batching: at step s pick a still-present matching pair P_t, pick a witness row E_s containing it, and remove B_s = {u : P_u still present and P_u cap E_s nonempty}, a_s = |B_s| (tag 10). With V_s the union of pair endpoints in B_s and U_s = E_s cap V_s: the U_s are pairwise disjoint, E_s contains at least a_s+1 coordinates of U_s, and E_t cap U_s = empty for t < s. Conditioning on coordinates outside the union of U_s and peeling U_k,...,U_1 in reverse gives Pr(h_s.X in {+-1} | earlier) <= psi(a_s+1) (tag 11), hence 2^{-ell} <= prod_s psi(a_s+1) (tag 13).
notes: S7 confirms this is a triangular CONDITIONAL-EXPECTATION product, not an independence claim, and requires the proof be rewritten with the disjoint U_s and an explicit reverse conditional expectation. Rows E_s may still involve variables in earlier U_t; those are held as arbitrary parameters, which is why target uniformity is needed.

name: batching_entropy_arithmetic
statement: Put c_s = -log_2 psi(a_s+1). Then c_s >= beta := log_2(4/3), sum_s c_s <= ell, and a_s+1 <= 4*4^{c_s} (tag 14). With C_* = sum_s c_s and b = 4^beta = 16/9, (sum_s 4^{c_s})/4^{C_*} = sum_s 4^{-(C_*-c_s)} <= m*b^{-(m-1)} <= 9/8 (tag 15), maximized at m = 2 and equal to 1 at m = 1. Since C_* <= ell this gives N = sum_s a_s <= (9/2)*4^ell (tag 16), and taking the matching endpoints as C gives |C| = 2N <= 9*4^ell.
source: dossier p.117 (S6 lines 194-222); audit pp.132-133 (S7 lines 187-235)
notes: m is the number of batches. Monotonicity check (S7): (m+1)b^{-m} / (m b^{-(m-1)}) = (m+1)/(mb) < 1 for m >= 2. The N = 0 case must be separated before the weighted sum. The key gain over the old proof: a dense row meeting many matching pairs is charged its full O(a_s^{-1/2}) LO atom instead of one 3/4 factor times its support size.

name: entropy_sharpened_star_core_thm2
statement: Theorem 2 (S6). Assume in addition that S is antipodal and nonempty. For the fixed input coordinate basis, d(H) <= C_0*4^ell + ell (tag 17). Consequently, for a full-closed fibre, d_cb(A) <= C_0*4^{ell(A)} + ell(A) (tag 18).
source: dossier pp.117-118 (S6 lines 229-242); audit pp.134-135 (S7 lines 240-301)
notes: Improves the old residual-rank bound |C| + 2^{|C|} to |C| + ell. With C_0 = 9 this reads d(H) <= 9*4^ell + ell. No full-closure assumption is used except when (18) is read as a statement about the entire full dual. S7: antipodality is automatic for a nonempty compatibility set defined by homogeneous two-sided constraints h_a.x in {+-1}.

name: conditionally_free_coordinate_dichotomy
statement: After Theorem 1 each row is h_a(x) = q_a(x_C) + lambda_a*x_j for at most one j outside C (tag 19). Call j conditionally free if for SOME realized core value X_C = c both signs of X_j occur among points of S having that same core value. If a row uses a conditionally free j, evaluating on two such points gives q_a(c)+lambda_a and q_a(c)-lambda_a both in {+-1}; since lambda_a is nonzero these are the two distinct signs, so q_a(c) = 0 and lambda_a = +-1 (tag 20). Assign the row to the signed coordinate lambda_a*x_j; its residual is supported on C.
source: dossier p.118 (S6 lines 246-271); audit p.134 (S7 lines 243-262)
notes: 'Distinct' requires characteristic zero or odd characteristic - this is where the odd-p hypothesis enters Theorem 2 (as opposed to Theorem 1, where it enters via LO).

name: never_free_vector_determinism_N0_bound
statement: Let N_0 be the outside coordinates that are never conditionally free. For every realized core pattern each X_j, j in N_0, has at most one possible sign, so the WHOLE VECTOR X_{N_0} (not merely each coordinate separately) is a deterministic function of X_C: H(X_C, X_{N_0}) = H(X_C) (tag 21). For uniform X on S, r - ell = H(X) <= H(X_C) + r - |C| - |N_0| (tag 22), hence |N_0| <= ell - (|C| - H(X_C)) <= ell (tag 23).
source: dossier pp.118-119 (S6 lines 273-301); audit p.134 (S7 lines 263-283)
notes: S6 flags this explicitly: 'This is the point at which a naive conditioning argument can go wrong. Equation (21) is valid precisely because never free is required for EVERY realized core pattern.' A per-coordinate version of the argument is false.

name: conditional_exponential_cyclic_block_thm3
statement: Theorem 3 (S6), the connector-ready but exponential estimate. Let (W,Q) be a sign basis on a finite support A with |Q| = q and L = q - H(Q|W) (tag 24). Let Y_a be sign-valued linear forms with private decomposition Y_a = u_a(W) + h_a(Q) (tag 25); boundary-only forms are passed to the parent. There is a private coordinate set C with |C| <= C_0*4^L such that every supp h_a has at most one coordinate outside C, and the private forms admit selectors whose NEW residual rank modulo span W is at most C_0*4^L + L (tag 26).
notes: Proof route: L = E_w[q - log_2|A_w|] (27); choose w_0 with fibre defect <= L; the compatibility set cut out by u_a(w_0)+h_a(Q) in {+-1} contains A_{w_0}, so has density >= 2^{-L}; Theorem 1 is target-uniform and applies VERBATIM to these affine equations. Free/never-free then gives H(Q_{N_0}|W,Q_C) = 0 (28) and |N_0| <= L. Not separately audited by S7 (S7 audits Theorems 1-2 only).

name: thm3_does_not_give_absorption
statement: Theorem 3 does NOT prove (3). It bounds the quotient rank, but a linear combination of the chosen residuals may fall completely into the boundary and create a new, unpaid connector direction. That is exactly the absorption gap isolated in the recursive block-tree theorem.
notes: The precise failure mode: quotient-rank control says nothing about which combinations land in span W. S9's Lemma 2 turns this into an exact kernel criterion.

name: endpoint_component_exponent_ternary_basis_mass
statement: For a rank-r, size-k = r+j component, the ternary basis-mass encoding has exponent -(n-r)*ell + O(d_cb*k + j*log r + r + n) (tag 29). Substituting Theorem 2 gives -(n-r)*ell + O((4^ell + ell)*k + j*log r + r + n) (tag 30).
source: dossier pp.120-121 (S6 lines 392-404); audit p.136 (S7 lines 339-343)
notes: This is the exact interface at which a deterministic d_cb bound becomes a probabilistic component saving; the coefficient on d_cb is k (component size), which is why an o(log n) coefficient suffices at the endpoint.

name: controlled_range_4l_o_ell_log_n
statement: Uniformly for k = O(n/log n), every component sequence with ell -> infinity and 4^ell = o(ell*log n) (tag 31) has the required exponential component saving: (29) equals -(1-o(1))*(n-r)*ell. Fixed defect was already covered by the star-core theorem.
source: dossier p.121 (S6 lines 405-414); audit verification pp.136-137 (S7 lines 344-377)
notes: S7's explicit arithmetic: r,j <= k gives n-r = n(1-o(1)) and j log r + r + n = O(n); (4^ell+ell)k/((n-r)ell) = O(4^ell/(ell log n) + 1/log n) = o(1); (j log r + r + n)/((n-r)ell) = O(1/ell) = o(1).

name: survivor_defect_threshold_loglog
statement: Pointwise form (S7): if for some fixed c > 0 one has 4^ell/(ell*log n) >= c (tag 35), then 2*ell >= log_2 log n + log_2 ell - O_c(1) (36) and hence ell >= (1/2)log_2 log n + (1/2)log_2 log log n - O_c(1) (37). Equivalently and unambiguously (38): ell <= (1/2)log_2 log n + (1/2)log_2 log log n - omega(1) implies 4^ell = o(ell log n).
source: dossier p.121 (S6 lines 415-421); corrected form pp.137-138 (S7 lines 379-409)
notes: QUANTIFIER CORRECTION, required by S7: S6's tag (32) as written is wrong for oscillating sequences. Failure of the little-o condition only yields c > 0 and an INFINITE SUBSEQUENCE on which (35), hence (37), holds - not the threshold at every index. Cite the pointwise (35) or the subsequence form, never (32) unqualified.

name: improvement_over_unweighted_core_estimate
statement: The previous unweighted core estimate only reached (1+ell)*4^ell = o(log n); the weighted batching reaches 4^ell = o(ell log n), gaining the missing polynomial factors in ell. This is a real extension of the controlled range, but it does not cover the full possible interval ell*(n-r) < r*j + O(n).
source: dossier p.121 (S6 lines 422-427); also p.115 (S6 lines 99-101)
notes: Also records the two structural improvements of Theorem 1/2 over the older proof: core size O((1+ell)4^ell) -> O(4^ell), residual rank |C| + 2^{|C|} -> |C| + ell.

name: cex_rank_seven_all_11_shared_slice
statement: The rank-seven all-(1,1) shared slice has ell = log_2(16/7) and d_cb = 2, although EVERY pairwise potential recurrence fails. Theorems 1-2 survive it because they use a simultaneous support matching and no one-pair recurrence.
notes: Counterexample-audit item 2. Refutes any proof that tries to propagate rigidity via pairwise potential recurrences.

name: cex_k33_incremental_rigidity
statement: K_{3,3} incremental obstruction: adding the ninth form raises rigidity from one to two while deleting only one antipodal pair (mass ratio 7/8). Hence no deletion-ratio assertion (rigidity increment forces a proportional loss of fibre mass) is available. General K_{p,q} grids also satisfy (17), albeit nonsharply.
notes: Counterexample-audit item 3. Kills deletion-ratio / sequential-rigidity-increment proof strategies; S6's Theorems 1-2 make no such assertion.

name: failed_saturated_optimizer_k3q
statement: Saturated-optimizer failures in K_{3,q}: there is no saturated geometric optimizer and no private collision to invoke. Any proof asking for one fails on this family.
notes: Counterexample-audit item 4. S6's proof deliberately avoids both devices.

name: cex_32_star_treewidth_two_family
statement: The (3,2)-star / treewidth-two family: its density tends to 1/2 while the number of ears is unbounded, yet its actual residual rank remains ONE. The weighted batching survives it by putting all matching pairs met by the shared dense row into one batch and charging that batch its true Littlewood-Offord atom.
notes: Counterexample-audit item 5. This family is exactly why the batching must be WEIGHTED: an unweighted charge of one 3/4 factor per dense row times its support size loses here.

name: crosspolytope_excess_dual_useless
statement: Crosspolytopes: their full dual has exponentially many forms, so excess-dual (dual-cardinality) bounds are useless on them. Here ell = r - Theta(log r), so the exponential bound (17) is intentionally much weaker than the exact crosspolytope certificate and causes no contradiction.
notes: Counterexample-audit item 6. Records that the crosspolytope does not contradict (17) - the contradiction it does produce is against the O(m) residual bootstrap (see one_witness_per_batch_bootstrap_false).

name: failed_axis_subcube_and_sequential_increment
statement: Balanced middle slices and the maximum-axis-subcube failure: no proof may use an axis-aligned subcube extraction or a sequential rigidity increment. S6's argument uses neither.
notes: Counterexample-audit item 7.

name: failed_direct_sum_additivity_of_dcb
statement: Arbitrary direct-sum additivity of d_cb on abstract coordinate families is not available. S6's proof establishes a single GLOBAL residual span instead of assuming additivity.
notes: Counterexample-audit item 8. Relevant to any block-decomposition/telescope argument that wants to add per-block residual ranks.

name: random_dense_row_exponential_barrier
statement: A single row of support s has two-point atom O(s^{-1/2}), so its defect is at least (1/2)log_2 s - O(1) - exactly the scale s = O(4^ell) appearing in (8). Hence the exponential dependence in Theorems 1-2 CANNOT be improved by a support-size argument alone; a linear theorem must use basis exchange or aggregation of the residual row space.
notes: One of the sharpest constraints on the whole program: it names the only two admissible mechanisms for reaching linear-in-defect (basis exchange, residual-row-space aggregation) and rules out support/density counting. Consistency check for the two-shadow theorem, not a counterexample.

name: residual_class_after_thm3
statement: The unresolved deterministic statement is confined to blocks with ALL of: singleton-layer cyclic SCC after every admissible Gale basis exchange; in the homogeneous boundary-closed case relation corank >= 5; in the nonroot case genuinely affine boundary fibres and failure of connector absorption; conditional defect satisfying the threshold (32) while the general basis-mass estimate forces ell*(n-r) < r*j + O(n); no sparse-cyclomatic fundamental graph, no relation-side feedback set of size o(log n), no large disjoint-support matching, no o(log n) ordinary star core, no sufficiently low-rank shared form, and no multiplicative subgroup/coset fibre.
notes: This is the exact residual class the open theorem must cover. Every exclusion is a route already closed elsewhere in the dossier; a candidate counterexample or proof must respect all of them simultaneously.

name: high_corank_connector_rigidity_theorem
statement: THE NAMED GAP (boxed in S6). High-corank connector-rigidity theorem: every cyclic SCC in the residual class has a globally compatible basis/selector certificate satisfying (3), with an ABSOLUTE LINEAR coefficient. Equivalently, one may bypass the decomposition and prove the global selector theorem (1), or the stronger Rado theorem (4), directly. S6: 'This is the irreducible gap: not another scalar endpoint enumeration, but a mass/entropy-weighted basis-exchange theorem for a genuinely high-corank cyclic two-level configuration.'
notes: The coefficient must be at least 2.40942 by the NAE three-circuit products. Proving it is still NOT the conjecture - the Layer-III transfer remains separate.

name: low_corank_induction_does_not_lift
statement: The finite corank-three/four classifications verify only the first local cases of the connector-rigidity assertion and do NOT imply it by induction, for two named reasons: (i) one-new-form ears have zero local rank-corrected entropy, and (ii) nonbinary separator states do not factor.
notes: These two reasons are the concrete obstructions any inductive lift must defeat; a proposed induction that does not address zero-entropy ears and nonbinary separators is already known to fail.

name: simultaneous_pivot_triangular_exchange
statement: Number the batches in deletion order, let h_s be the witness form at batch s, and choose a pivot p_s from the witness matching pair in B_s. Then h_s(p_s) != 0 and h_s(p_t) = 0 for t > s (tag 33), because every pair in a later batch was still present when h_s was chosen so h_s cannot meet either of its endpoints. Hence T = (h_s(p_t))_{1<=s,t<=m} (34) is triangular with nonzero diagonal, and B' = {h_1,...,h_m} union {x_j : j not in {p_1,...,p_m}} (35) is an admissible coordinate basis.
notes: S6: 'This simultaneous exchange lemma is completely correct.' What it does NOT say is that another row is close, modulo a low-rank space, to a member of B'; triangularity concerns only the m-by-m pivot minor of the selected witnesses.

name: walsh_hadamard_fibre_full_closure
statement: Let r = 2^{2t} with coordinates indexed by F_2^{2t}, H the symmetric Walsh-Hadamard matrix H_{a,z} = (-1)^{a.z} with H^2 = rI, and c_z = H e_z in {+-1}^r. The antipodal spanning fibre A_r = {+- c_z} (tag 36) has signed full dual D~(A_r) = {h_v = (1/r)Hv : v in {+-1}^r} (37), with h_v.c_z = v_z (38). A_r is FULLY CLOSED: if x in {+-1}^r satisfies every equation of (37), then y = H^T x has v.y in {+-r} for all sign vectors v (39), so comparing v with its i-th flip gives y_i in {0,+-r}; since ||y||^2 = r||x||^2 = r^2 exactly one coordinate is nonzero, hence x = +- c_z.
notes: The crosspolytope family in its exact form. Full closure is PROVED here, not assumed - this is what makes it admissible as a counterexample against statements quantified over full-closed fibres. |A_r| = 2r, so ell = r - log_2(2r) = r - Theta(log r).

name: bent_quadratic_full_support_dual_form
statement: Take the bent quadratic q(z) = sum_{i=1}^t z_i z_{t+i} and v_z = (-1)^{q(z)} (tag 40). For a = (alpha,beta) in F_2^t x F_2^t the Walsh transform factors as (Hv)_a = prod_{i=1}^t sum_{u,w in F_2} (-1)^{uw + alpha_i u + beta_i w}, which lies in {+-2^t} (41). Hence the admissible full-dual form h_v = r^{-1}Hv has FULL support, the two-shadow graph is complete, and choosing h_v as the witness for the first pair of any perfect matching gives m = 1 batch (42), with nonzero coefficient at either endpoint so the exchange (35) is admissible.
notes: The bentness is what forces every Walsh coefficient to be nonzero, hence full support. This single-batch configuration is the engine of the O(m)-bootstrap refutation.

name: crosspolytope_selector_residual_lower_bound
statement: After the one-batch exchange on A_r, every signed-selector residual certificate has dimension d >= r - floor(log_2(2r)) (tag 43). Proof: let R be the residual span and pi the quotient map of rank q = r - d. Selector feasibility says every member of D~(A_r) has the same quotient image, up to sign, as one of the r members of the exchanged basis, so |pi(D~(A_r))| <= 2r (44). But (37) is an invertible linear image of the r-cube, and every rank-q linear image of a cube has at least 2^q distinct points (pick q input directions with independent images, fix the other signs, vary those q). Hence 2^{r-d} = 2^q <= 2r.
notes: For r = 2^{2t} the bound is r - (2t+1) while the number of batches remains ONE. The cube-image counting step (every rank-q linear image of a cube has >= 2^q points) is a reusable tool.

name: one_witness_per_batch_bootstrap_false
statement: The proposed inference 'one exchanged witness per batch implies residual rank O(m)' (tag 45) is FALSE, even for antipodal, spanning, fully closed REAL sign fibres. In the Walsh-Hadamard example the one selected dense equation certifies only an O(r^{-1/2}) Littlewood-Offord atom whereas the actual fibre density is 2r/2^r; the batching proof is intentionally allowed to leave almost all of that entropy defect unused, and the unselected full-dual rows retain r - O(log r) independent quotient complexity that triangular exchange does not see.
notes: S6's closing line: 'Pivot triangularity supplies basis admissibility and nothing stronger.' This is the sharpest known refutation of the dense-witness bootstrap and must be respected by any replacement argument.

name: bootstrap_repair_requirement
statement: A successful bootstrap would have to charge additional exchanges or residual directions to the REMAINING entropy defect after each batch, or prove a new quotient-class aggregation theorem. The refutation does not rule out deliberately choosing many SPARSE witnesses - the crosspolytope admits such choices with a number of batches of order r. It rules out entropy-efficient DENSE batching followed by an O(m) residual claim.
notes: Names the two surviving repair directions precisely, and preserves the sparse-witness escape hatch (which is what S9's bounded-congestion theorem exploits).

name: audit_verdict_thm1_thm2_pass
statement: S7 verdict: PASS, with two required wording/quantifier corrections. The weighted two-shadow compression theorem and the entropy-sharpened star-core rigidity theorem are correct; the triangular batching argument does give a product of conditional Littlewood-Offord factors and no independence of the selected constraint events is assumed. No dependency, exposure, Littlewood-Offord, or selector-rank counterexample was found.
notes: The two required corrections are (a) rewrite the reverse exposure with the disjoint U_s and explicit conditional expectation, (b) replace 'there is no cyclic wrap' by the finite-group one-point Littlewood-Offord theorem; plus the endpoint-threshold quantifier fix. This is an audit by a second agent reading the same project, NOT an independent re-derivation from primary sources.

name: disjoint_Us_structural_facts
statement: Five exact facts about the batching. (1) The batches B_s partition the matching edges, so the V_s are disjoint. (2) Hence the U_s = E_s cap V_s are pairwise disjoint. (3) |U_s| >= a_s + 1 (tag 6): the witness edge contributes both endpoints and each of the other a_s - 1 edges in B_s contributes at least one distinct endpoint. (4) E_t cap U_s = empty for t < s (tag 7): had E_t met an endpoint of a still-present edge of B_s, that edge would have been removed at stage t. (5) E_s meets no endpoint belonging to a later batch, so after fixing coordinates outside the union of the U_s, the indicator of the s-th selected constraint is a function of X_{U_1},...,X_{U_s} only (tag 8).
notes: The proof uses U_s, NOT the larger V_s - S7 states this explicitly. These five facts are the exact structural content the harness re-verifies by brute force.

name: reverse_conditional_expectation_identity
statement: Put Z = X restricted to the complement of the union of the U_s, Y_s = X_{U_s}, I_s = 1{h_s.X in {+-1}}. The blocks Y_1,...,Y_m,Z are mutually independent and I_s is measurable w.r.t. sigma(Z,Y_1,...,Y_s). Choosing any a_s+1 active coordinates in U_s and conditioning additionally on the rest of U_s turns the selected equation into a nonzero (a_s+1)-term Rademacher sum required to hit two arbitrary targets, so E[I_s | Z=z, Y_1,...,Y_{s-1}] <= psi(a_s+1) uniformly (tag 9). Reversing the blocks gives E[prod_s I_s | Z=z] <= prod_s psi(a_s+1) (10), hence 2^{-ell} = Pr(X in S) <= Pr(all I_s = 1) <= prod_s psi(a_s+1) (11).
notes: The |U_s| > a_s+1 case is handled by conditioning on the extra active coordinates BEFORE applying the (a_s+1)-term bound and averaging afterwards. S7: 'It does not assert that the events I_s = 1 are independent.'

name: two_target_three_quarter_bound
statement: After fixing all parameters outside a selected active set of size u, the event is sum_{i=1}^u c_i*eps_i in {b-1, b+1} with all c_i nonzero and b arbitrary (tag 12). For any two active coordinates, condition on the other u-2 signs: the four sums +-c_1 +- c_2 cannot all lie in a fixed two-point set when c_1,c_2 are nonzero. They have fewer than three distinct elements only if c_1 = +-c_2, in which case they are 0, 2c_1, -2c_1 up to translation - still three distinct values over R and over F_p with odd p > 2. Hence at most three of the four assignments work and the probability is <= 3/4 (13).
notes: Target-uniform and valid in every odd characteristic. This is the u = 2 branch of psi and the only branch that survives when u is small.

name: finite_group_one_point_LO
statement: Over R, sup_y Pr(sum_{i=1}^u c_i*eps_i = y) <= 2^{-u}*C(u, floor(u/2)) (tag 14). Over F_p the same inequality holds for nonzero coefficients when u < p - the finite-group Littlewood-Offord theorem in the no-wrap range (the F_p specialization of the optimal group inequality of Juskevicius-Semetulskis). In the application u <= r < p (15). Since p is odd the two targets b-1, b+1 are distinct, so applying (14) to each and taking a union bound gives <= 2^{1-u}*C(u, floor(u/2)) (16).
notes: [EXTRACTION-UNCERTAIN] the surname prints as 'JuskeviIius' in the text extraction; it is almost certainly Juskevicius (Juskevicius-Semetulskis). The hypothesis 'every nonzero coefficient has order p > u' is what licenses the central-binomial value.

name: no_cyclic_wrap_wording_is_not_a_proof
statement: The sentence 'the finite-field statement is valid because u < p, so there is no cyclic wrap' is NOT by itself a proof for arbitrary coefficients in F_p: arbitrary field coefficients can wrap numerically. What is true is that the optimal finite-group concentration theorem attains the central-binomial value when every nonzero coefficient has order p > u.
source: dossier pp.132-133 (S7 lines 184-185); correction 2 at p.138 (S7 line 414)
notes: A wording defect with real content: any future write-up must cite the finite-group theorem rather than argue by absence of wrap.

name: C0_equals_9_sharpening
statement: The endpoints of a maximum matching form a vertex cover of the two-shadow graph (a maximum matching is maximal), so |C| = 2N <= 9*4^ell (tag 22), and no support E_a can contain two vertices outside C since that pair would be an uncovered two-shadow edge. This proves Theorem 1 with the stronger admissible numerical choice C_0 = 9 (hence certainly with C_0 = 32).
notes: Use C_0 = 9 in any downstream computation; S6's C_0 = 32 is the safe-but-loose value. The N = 0 case must be separated before invoking the weighted sum (20).

name: thm2_edge_cases_and_antipodality
statement: Theorem 2 audit: correct, with edge cases to be stated. If C = empty then a noncoordinate row of support >= 2 would create a two-shadow edge and a nonempty matching, so no such core-only row exists. Discarded coordinate rows assign to themselves with zero residual. For a full-closed fibre, taking the rows to be its entire projective full dual makes their compatibility set exactly S; adding the input basis rows costs zero residual rank, and optimizing over coordinate bases gives the d_cb bound. Antipodality is harmless and in fact AUTOMATIC for a nonempty compatibility set defined by homogeneous two-sided constraints h_a.x in {+-1}. Final: d(H) <= |C| + |N_0| <= 9*4^ell + ell (28).
notes: No additional closure hypothesis is used inside the fixed-basis argument; full closure enters only when reinterpreting d(H) as d_cb over the whole full dual.

name: endpoint_arithmetic_o1_verification
statement: Under k = O(n/log n), ell -> infinity and 4^ell = o(ell log n) (tag 30): since r,j <= k one has n - r = n(1-o(1)) and j*log r + r + n = O(n) (31); (4^ell + ell)*k / ((n-r)*ell) = O(4^ell/(ell log n) + 1/log n) = o(1) (32); (j*log r + r + n)/((n-r)*ell) = O(1/ell) = o(1) (33). Hence the component exponent equals -(1-o(1))*(n-r)*ell (34).
notes: This is the arithmetic a transfer-lane argument must reuse when substituting a different coefficient for d_cb; note the coefficient enters multiplied by k and divided by (n-r)*ell.

name: six_required_corrections
statement: S7's exact correction list for the global bridge report: (1) replace the reverse-exposure paragraph of Theorem 1 by the U_s / conditional-expectation equations (5)-(11); (2) replace the no-cyclic-wrap sentence by the finite-group one-point Littlewood-Offord lemma plus the two-target union bound; (3) state that when |U_s| > a_s+1 the extra active coordinates are conditioned before applying the (a_s+1)-term bound; (4) separate the trivial N = 0 case before the weighted sum; (5) in Theorem 2 state how core-only rows are assigned, including the C = empty edge case; (6) qualify the lower-threshold conclusion as pointwise under (35) or as an infinite-subsequence conclusion.
notes: S7's closing sentence: with these corrections Theorems 1-2 and the controlled endpoint range are rigorous, but 'They remain exponential in ell and therefore do not close the high-corank connector-rigidity problem identified elsewhere in the report.'

name: harness_global_exponential_audit_checks
statement: The adversarial checker global_exponential_audit_checks.py (path /workspace/scratch/682eb2738f23/) uses exact integer/Fraction arithmetic to search for counterexamples to the triangular batching/exposure inequality and to the finite-field two-target Littlewood-Offord quantifiers. It implements psi(u) = min(3/4, 2*C(u,floor(u/2))/2^u), an exact maximum matching by memoized DP over vertex masks, a canonical greedy batching, exact rational rank, and full sign-cube enumeration.
source: dossier pp.139-144 (S8 lines 1-271); described at p.135 (S7 lines 306-311)
notes: S8 docstring: 'The searches are not used as proofs. They are exact counterexample searches.' Reproduction command: python3 global_exponential_audit_checks.py.

name: numeric_finite_field_lo_pass
statement: Checker output line: FINITE_FIELD_LO PASS coefficient_multisets=4370 u=2..8 primes<=13,p>u. The search ranges over u = 2..8, primes p in {3,5,7,11,13} with p > u, and all coefficient multisets in {1,...,(p-1)/2} of size u (exhaustive because sign changes and permutations preserve the distribution). For each it forms the exact frequency table of sum a_i*x_i mod p over all 2^u sign patterns, takes worst = max over centers of freq[(center-1) mod p] + freq[(center+1) mod p], and asserts worst <= min(3*2^u//4, 2*C(u,floor(u/2))).
source: dossier p.144 (S8 lines 241-260); output at p.135 (S8 line 330 / S7 line 313)
notes: FINITE WINDOW ONLY: u <= 8, p <= 13. It is evidence for psi in odd characteristic, not a proof; the proof is the finite-group Littlewood-Offord theorem. 4370 is the exact number of coefficient classes checked.

name: numeric_batching_pass
statement: Checker output line: BATCHING PASS exhaustive_systems=14592 random_systems=5000. Exhaustive part: every system of up to three normalized ternary rows in rank four and every system of up to two such rows in rank five (14,592 systems), where a normalized ternary row has entries in {-1,0,1}, support at least two, and first nonzero entry +1. Random part: 5,000 seeded systems (random.Random(20260815)) in ranks five through nine, with up to seven rows and coefficients in {+-1,+-2}.
source: dossier pp.143-144 (S8 lines 213-238); output at p.135 (S8 line 331 / S7 lines 314-315)
notes: FINITE WINDOW ONLY: ranks 4-5 exhaustively over ternary rows, ranks 5-9 by a seeded random sample. No claim of exhaustiveness beyond that; the random half is a sample, not a certificate over its range.

name: harness_stagewise_and_conditional_checks
statement: For every system the harness reconstructs a maximum matching, the batches and the actual U_s, then asserts: |U_s| >= |B_s| + 1; the U_s are pairwise disjoint; supp(E_t) cap U_s = empty for t < s; original_count <= selected_count; the global bound selected_count/2^r <= prod_s psi(|B_s|+1); the same product bound CONDITIONAL on EVERY assignment outside the union of the U_s; and every stagewise inequality count/2^{|U_s|} <= psi(|B_s|+1) for every assignment of the earlier U_t and of all other fixed coordinates.
notes: The conditional versions are the load-bearing checks: they test the reverse-exposure inequality pointwise in the conditioning, which is exactly the quantifier S7 required be made explicit.

name: harness_theorem2_selector_check
statement: On every nonempty compatibility set the harness takes C = the matching endpoints, computes the free / never-free partition of the outside coordinates (j is free iff some realized core pattern admits both signs of x_j among accepted points), asserts the deterministic cardinality inequality 2^{|N_0|} * |S| <= 2^r (equivalently |N_0| <= ell), builds the Theorem-2 selectors (signed coefficient for free j, +1 for never-free j, a core coordinate for core-only rows), and asserts the exact rational bound rank(residuals) <= |C| + |N_0|.
notes: 2^{|N_0|}*|S| <= 2^r is the exact CARDINALITY form of the entropy step (23), since |S| = 2^{r-ell}; useful as a cheap deterministic surrogate when auditing new families. Residual rank is computed in exact Fraction arithmetic.

name: harness_canonical_greedy_batching_scope
statement: The harness's make_batches implements ONE canonical allowed greedy batching (docstring: 'One canonical allowed greedy batching'): it always takes the lowest-index still-present matching pair and the lowest-index row containing it as witness. It does not enumerate all admissible greedy orders, witness choices, or maximum matchings.
notes: Scope caveat that matters when quoting BATCHING PASS: the checks certify the inequalities for that batching, which is enough for Theorem 1 (it needs only one displayed certificate) but is not a search over batchings - relevant if one later wants to MINIMIZE congestion kappa, which does quantify over batchings.

name: harness_evidence_scope_caveat
statement: S7 on its own searches: 'These searches are corroboration, not a replacement for Sections 2-5.' The finite-window results (u <= 8, p <= 13; ranks 4-5 exhaustive over ternary rows; ranks 5-9 sampled) may not be cited as proof of Theorems 1-2 or of psi in odd characteristic.
notes: Honesty boundary between the finite certificates and the analytic proof; keep it attached whenever the PASS counts are quoted.

name: bounded_congestion_verdict_constants
statement: S9 verdict. There is a rigorous linear-in-defect theorem for the part of the high-corank problem in which the weighted two-shadow batching has bounded entropy-normalized exposure congestion kappa. It is conditional, works on affine boundary fibres, uses the conditional defect that the dense-witness exchange leaves unused, and controls ALL unselected rows. In the original junction basis the constant is 2*kappa+1. If selected witnesses have private support at most s then kappa <= (s-1)/beta with beta = log_2(4/3), giving new quotient residual rank <= (1 + 2(s-1)/beta)*L (tag 1); insisting on the triangularly exchanged witness basis raises the constant by only beta^{-1}, to (1 + (2s-1)/beta)*L (tag 2).
notes: S9: 'This is a genuine residual-compression result, not the false inference that one residual direction is enough per selected witness.' Conditional on bounded kappa, which is precisely what the residual class (congestion >~ log n in every useful basis) denies.

name: rooted_setup_S9
statement: K = R, or K = F_p with odd p > q. (W,Q) is a sign basis on a finite support A with private part Q = (Q_1,...,Q_q). Set B = span_K W, R_< subset B, and L = q - H(Q|W) (tag 3). Private forms are Y_a = u_a(W) + h_a(Q) with Y_a(A) subset {+-1} (4), and E_a = supp h_a. Boundary-only forms are passed to the parent. Singleton private supports are RETAINED but do not create two-shadow edges. The private two-shadow graph has edge ij whenever some E_a contains both i and j.
notes: The retention of singleton private supports is what lets the NAE-star counterexample have an EMPTY two-shadow graph while still having forms to select - do not silently discard them.

name: exposure_congestion_kappa
statement: With c_s = -log_2 psi(a_s+1) >= beta = log_2(4/3), the exposure congestion of a batching is kappa(B) = max_s a_s/c_s (tag 6); when N = 0, kappa := 0. Sufficient hypotheses: if every selected witness meets at most D still-present matching pairs then kappa <= D/beta; if every selected witness has private support at most s then a_s+1 <= |E_s| <= s so kappa <= (s-1)/beta; if the two-shadow graph has maximum degree Delta then each row support spans a clique of size at most Delta+1, so kappa <= Delta/beta.
notes: kappa may be MINIMIZED over the choice of maximum matching, witness row and greedy order, but the theorem needs only ONE displayed batching certificate. S9 stresses it is strictly more flexible than a row-support bound - it is the number of pairs killed per BIT of entropy charged, not per row.

name: bounded_congestion_residual_compression_S9_thm1
statement: S9 Theorem 1. In the rooted setup, a coordinate-selector certificate R exists with dim((R+B)/B) <= (2*kappa+1)*L (tag 7), where kappa is the congestion of any one certified batching. No full-closure and no antipodality hypothesis is needed. Proof: L = E_w[q - log_2|A_w|] (8); pick w_0 with q - log_2|A_{w_0}| <= L so the affine compatibility set has density >= 2^{-L}; reverse exposure gives 2^{-L} <= prod psi(a_s+1), i.e. sum_s c_s <= L (10); then N = sum a_s <= kappa*sum c_s <= kappa*L (11), |C| = 2N <= 2*kappa*L (12); free/never-free gives lambda_a = +-1 (13) and |N_0| <= L (15); all residual private projections lie in P_0 = span Q_{C union N_0} with dim P_0 <= (2kappa+1)L (16); project along B.
notes: S9 marks the exact step (line 163-164): 'This is precisely where the conditional entropy defect, rather than an unconditional block defect, is used.' The edge case C = empty is harmless: a core-only row is then boundary-only and already passed to the parent. Not separately audited by S7 (which covers S6 only).

name: unrooted_bounded_support_linear_rank_bound
statement: For an unrooted homogeneous fibre B = 0, so S9 Theorem 1 is already a true residual rank bound: if selected witness private support is at most s then d(H) <= (1 + 2(s-1)/beta)*ell (tag 17), beta = log_2(4/3).
notes: S9: 'Unlike the invalid one-direction-per-batch bootstrap, this proof controls every unselected row through the matching vertex cover and the free/never-free entropy dichotomy.' This is a genuine LINEAR-in-defect theorem, but only under bounded witness support.

name: witness_exchange_costs_L_over_beta
statement: With m batches, choosing one pivot p_s per witness pair and replacing Q_{p_s} by the sign-valued witness Y_s, the pivot matrix is triangular modulo B with nonzero diagonal, so (W, Y_1,...,Y_m, Q_j for j not a pivot) (tag 18) is an admissible sign basis. For each fixed boundary value it is an invertible change of private coordinates, hence preserves H(Q|W) and L. From sum c_s <= L and c_s >= beta, m <= L/beta (19). Keeping old selectors and adding the exchange discrepancies e_s = Q_{p_s} - Y_s (20) gives exchanged-basis quotient residual rank <= (2kappa+1)L + m <= (2kappa+1+beta^{-1})L (21).
notes: beta^{-1} = 1/log_2(4/3) = 2.40942 - the same constant as the NAE three-circuit floor, appearing here as the price of the exchange. The invariance of L under the exchange is what makes the charge additive rather than multiplicative.

name: crosspolytope_kappa_r_over_log_r
statement: The crosspolytope (Walsh-Hadamard) counterexample is consistent with S9 Theorem 1: its one dense batch has a_1 asymptotic to r and c_1 asymptotic to log r, so kappa is asymptotic to r/log r - unbounded. The (2kappa+1)L bound is therefore vacuous there, which is exactly why it does not contradict the r - O(log r) residual-rank lower bound.
notes: The reconciliation that makes bounded congestion the RIGHT hypothesis: the known counterexample lives exactly at unbounded kappa. Any attempt to remove the kappa hypothesis must explain this family.

name: lemma2_connector_factorization
statement: Write the chosen residual generators uniquely as r_a = b_a + p_a with b_a in B and p_a in P_0 (tag 22). Let F be the free coefficient space on the generators and define P: F -> P_0, e_a -> p_a, and Bbar: F -> B/R_<, e_a -> b_a + R_< (23). The following are EQUIVALENT: (1) R cap B subset R_<; (2) ker P subset ker Bbar; (3) there is a linear T: im P -> B/R_< with Bbar = T o P. Under them, dim((R+R_<)/R_<) = dim((R+B)/B) <= (2kappa+1)L (24).
notes: Proof: sum lambda_a r_a lies in B exactly when P*lambda = 0, and its boundary class mod R_< is Bbar*lambda (1 iff 2); the quotient factorization lemma gives (2 iff 3); the projection of (R+R_<)/R_< onto (R+B)/B is surjective with zero kernel under condition 1, hence an isomorphism. THIS IS THE EXACT ABSORPTION CRITERION - it converts an existential clause of target (3) into a checkable kernel containment.

name: exchanged_basis_augmented_kernel_test
statement: For the exchanged basis, apply Lemma 2 to the AUGMENTED residual list {r_a} union {e_s}. This is a convenient sufficient test and can be STRONGER THAN NECESSARY, because the actual transformed residuals may use only particular combinations of the e_s. If the augmented kernel condition holds, (21) becomes the full rooted bound dim((R+R_<)/R_<) <= (2kappa+1+beta^{-1})*L with R cap B subset R_< (tag 25).
notes: The over-strength of the augmented test is a live slack: a block failing it may still absorb. Relevant to anyone hunting counterexamples - failing the augmented test is not a counterexample to absorption.

name: absorption_structural_certificates
statement: Three small certificates for ker P subset ker Bbar. (a) PRIVATE ANCHORS: if the matrix of private residual projections has full column rank then ker P = 0; a triangular system of distinct private anchors proves this immediately. (b) GRAPHIC/NETWORK CYCLIC BLOCKS: if P is a scaled oriented incidence matrix then ker P is generated by fundamental cycles, so it suffices to verify that the signed boundary trace around each fundamental cycle lies in R_<; equivalently, modulo R_<, the connector labels are differences of vertex potentials. (c) BOUNDED DEPENDENCY BASIS: any displayed basis of ker P is a finite certificate - check its boundary trace under Bbar; this is the appropriate exact-arithmetic test for a finite normal-form block.
notes: For a bounded-support high-corank cyclic block, bounded congestion gives the linear rank charge while cycle closure gives absorption - the two hypotheses are independent and both needed. (b) is the concrete cohomological-flavoured test: connector labels must be exact as a potential difference mod R_<.

name: common_linear_lift_is_condition_3
statement: The 'common-linear-lift' language of recursive_paired_block_tree_entropy.md is PRECISELY condition 3 of Lemma 2: the existence of a linear T: im P -> B/R_< with Bbar = T o P.
notes: Load-bearing for the campaign: recursive_paired_block_tree_entropy.md is cited but NOT reproduced in the dossier and is absent from every machine this campaign controls, so this sentence plus S14's condition (14) is the entire surviving specification of its interface. S9 adds: Lemma 2 makes clear both what a witness-basis exchange must preserve and why pivot triangularity alone is insufficient.

name: nae_star_exact_counterexample
statement: Real sign coordinates W = (x_1,z_1,x_2,z_2,x_3,z_3), Q = (q) (tag 26), with three NAE forms Y_i = x_i + z_i + q, i = 1,2,3 (27), and A = {(W,q) in {+-1}^7 : Y_i in {+-1} for i = 1,2,3} (28). For fixed q each pair has exactly three allowed values, so |A| = 2*3^3 = 54 (29). The fibre is antipodal, spanning and fully closed. Both values of q occur at a fixed W exactly when all three pairs are opposite, mass 2*2^3/(2*3^3) = 8/27; otherwise q is determined. Hence H(q|W) = 8/27 and L = 19/27 (30). Every private support is the singleton {q}, private incidence degree is three, and the two-shadow graph is EMPTY. Selecting q for each Y_i gives residuals x_i+z_i: quotient residual rank mod B is ZERO while the unpaid boundary residual rank is THREE.
notes: Spanning is proved by fixing q = 1 and all pairs but one: the three allowed values of that pair are affinely spanning, forcing the two coefficients of any vanishing form to vanish, after which the coefficient of q vanishes. Full closure: the three displayed full-dual forms already cut out (28). The point: (7) can be EXTREMELY strong (bound 0) while absorption completely fails.

name: nae_star_full_dual_classification
statement: On the slice q = 1 the domain is the product of three copies of T = {(1,-1),(-1,1),(-1,-1)} (tag 31). If a linear sign-valued form has nonconstant contributions from two pair blocks, the sum of their two ranges has at least three real values, impossible for a {+-1}-valued form; so it uses at most one pair. Solving the three values on one NAE triple shows the projective possibilities are exactly q, x_i, z_i, Y_i (32). Consequently a sign basis retaining the incoming boundary W must take its one private member to be either q or one Y_j, up to sign.
notes: A complete classification of the full dual - this is what makes the impossibility argument exhaustive over boundary-preserving bases rather than merely over the obvious ones.

name: nae_star_no_boundary_preserving_repair
statement: No boundary-preserving admissible sign basis repairs the NAE-star absorption failure. Whatever the basis takes as its single private member (q, or one Y_j, up to sign), two of the three forms - call them Y_i, Y_k - remain, and for EVERY signed selector choice their residuals are linearly independent. Their span therefore has dimension at least 2 while its private projection has dimension at most 1, so the span contains a nonzero pure-boundary vector. With R_< = 0, connector absorption is impossible.
notes: Proof of the independence: the residual Y_i -/+ g retains at least one of the two boundary coordinates x_i, z_i private to that row; a residual from Y_k meets at most one of x_i, z_i, since a basis selector has at most one such boundary coordinate and the sole nonboundary basis form is supported on the j-th pair; if the two were proportional, the first would have to cancel one of its own pair coordinates by selecting it and would then have no support on x_k, z_k, while the second necessarily retains one - contradiction. Quantifier is over ALL boundary-preserving admissible sign bases AND all signed selector choices. R_< = 0 is essential: the leak is fatal only when ancestors have paid nothing.

name: nae_star_leak_to_defect_ratios
statement: Arithmetic consequences of the NAE-star numbers: with L = 19/27, the naive selection's unpaid boundary leak rank 3 gives leak/L = 81/19 = 4.263..., and the forced minimum of one pure-boundary leak direction gives leak/L >= 27/19 = 1.421.... Hence any LEAK-charging inequality of the form leak <= C''*L needs C'' >= 27/19 on this family, and >= 81/19 if the naive selection must also be covered.
notes: DERIVED BY THE DIGESTER from the source's exact numbers (L = 19/27 at tag 30, leak rank 3 at line 417-418, forced leak >= 1 at lines 455-457). These ratios are NOT printed in S9. They constrain a leak-charging route, not target (3) itself, which counts leak inside dim((R+R_<)/R_<).

name: nae_star_logical_role
statement: S9 on the scope of its counterexample: 'This example is a low-rank star, not one of the final cyclic SCC survivors. Its role is logical: bounded private row support, bounded private incidence degree, conditional defect, and basis optimization do not imply connector absorption. A cycle-kernel/common-lift condition, or some stronger structural replacement for it, is indispensable.'
notes: Guards against two misreadings: (a) that the star is a counterexample to the conjecture (it is not - it is outside the residual class), and (b) that some milder hypothesis than a coherence/lift condition could be found.

name: absorption_hypothesis_is_necessary
statement: Connector absorption does not follow from bounded support, overlap, or incidence degree: a fully closed spanning antipodal affine star with private support ONE and private incidence degree THREE has no absorbing signed-selector certificate for ANY boundary-preserving admissible sign basis. Hence a connector compatibility hypothesis is mathematically necessary. The exact useful hypothesis is the kernel/factorization certificate: every linear dependency among the private projections of the chosen residuals must have boundary trace already in the ancestor residual space; under it, (1) - or (2) after exchange - gives the full rooted estimate (3).
notes: S9's headline negative result. It forecloses any proof of target (3) that hopes to derive clause (ii) from local sparsity/degree data alone.

name: s9_integration_four_step_recipe
statement: The valid replacement for the residual-compression step: (1) exhibit a maximum-matching batching with bounded kappa (bounded witness support, matching overlap, or two-shadow degree suffices); (2) use S9 Theorem 1 to charge the ENTIRE unselected residual quotient to the conditional defect L; (3) if the witness exchange is required, add its at most L/beta discrepancy directions; (4) verify the connector kernel on a dependency basis, preferably a fundamental-cycle basis in a network-type cyclic block. Under these explicit hypotheses the block satisfies the rooted linear estimate needed by the recursive telescope.
notes: S9: 'Without step 4, even support-one, degree-three fully closed fibres fail the absorption statement.' The recipe covers bounded-support cyclic blocks whose connector labels close on a fundamental-cycle basis - in particular scaled graphic or network residual systems with paid cycle sums.

name: s9_final_open_problem
statement: S9's closing statement of the gap, verbatim in substance: the remaining open problem is to DERIVE such coherence, or an alternative global aggregation mechanism, for the genuinely dense high-corank cyclic SCCs, rather than ASSUME it. The bounded-congestion theorem does not solve the remaining dense, noncoherent singleton-layer SCC.
source: dossier p.155 (S9 lines 481-483); scope note p.146 (S9 lines 53-56)
notes: Note the explicit alternative offered by the source: an ALTERNATIVE GLOBAL AGGREGATION MECHANISM is an acceptable substitute for deriving coherence. That is the widest opening in the whole pp.113-155 range.
